blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: RGB-based video object segmentation (VOS) remains brittle under fast motion and adverse illumination. Event cameras preserve signal under blur and challenging exposure, but provide little evidence when motion slows. Interaction can restore object state for subsequent propagation, yet promptable event methods merely address single windows. We formalize event-based Promptable Video Segmentation (ePVS), where prompts at arbitrary windows initialize, correct, or introduce objects and predictions. We present Event Memory-As-Prompt Segmentation (E-MAPS), which transfers a pretrained promptable segmenter to event streams and learns propagation and correction. Event-to-Token (E2T) aligns recurrent event features with pretrained representations while preserving prompt-conditioning priors. Memory-Aware Prompting (MAP) converts object-conditioned history into sparse prompts, allowing memory and user inputs to share one decoder pathway efficiently. We construct Event-View Masklets (EViM) from 206K aligned RGB-event pairs and 620K masks for two-stage representation transfer and native event-video learning, and establish three training-disjoint benchmarks. E-MAPS leads prompt-once and interactive ePVS across all three benchmarks while being more efficient. It further demonstrates strong performance on zero-shot object tracking benchmarks. Project page: https://github.com/adonaydem/emaps-wacv

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Video Object Segmentation (VOS) aims to segment target objects across video frames while maintaining their identities [ 5 , 33 , 31 , 12 , 11 , 51 , 10 , 61 ] .
Despite strong progress, RGB-based methods can struggle with fast motion and difficult lighting, where blur and poor exposure weaken visual cues [ 62 , 17 , 43 , 9 , 53 , 26 , 64 , 28 , 14 , 24 ] .
Event cameras address some of these challenges by recording brightness changes with microsecond latency and high dynamic range [ 16 , 7 ] .
Yet their continuous, change-driven streams require efficient processing and may contain limited shape or identity cues during slow motion or low illumination [ 60 , 27 ] .
Tracking objects from events therefore requires maintaining identity through sparse activity, occlusion, and disappearance.
Promptable segmentation offers a flexible way to specify and correct objects using points, boxes, or masks [ 22 , 41 , 29 , 37 , 6 ] .
For event streams, we find that these prompts can also recover object state and guide subsequent propagation when observations are weak.
Existing Event-SAM adaptations mostly focus on individual windows or RGB–event fusion [ 9 , 53 , 24 , 14 ] , while event-only VOS has mainly supported initial-mask propagation without subsequent interaction [ 64 ] .
We therefore study an event-only setting that combines prompt-conditioned segmentation with temporal propagation in a single model.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Promptable Segmentation Foundation Models
blocks.zh: 2.1 快速分割基础模型

blocks.en:
Promptable segmentation allows users to specify and refine target objects through points, boxes, or masks [ 22 ] .
SAM established a flexible encoder–prompt–decoder architecture [ 22 ] , which TinySAM later made more efficient [ 41 ] .
Building on this foundation, SAM2 introduced streaming memory for video segmentation [ 37 ] , while SAM-I2V adapted image-based SAM models to promptable video tasks [ 29 ] .
Alongside these developments, VOS methods have relied on dense space–time memories to associate objects across frames and propagate their masks [ 31 , 12 , 11 , 51 , 10 , 61 ] .
E-MAPS builds on TinySAM’s compact semantic and prompt priors while learning temporal dynamics directly from event streams.
blocks.zh:
可快速分割允许用户通过点,框,或口罩来指定和精炼目标对象[22].
SAM建立了一个灵活的编码器–即时–解码器架构[22],TinySAM后来使这个架构更有效率[41].
在此基础上,SAM2引入了流传内存用于视频分割[37],而SAM-I2V则对基于图像的SAM模型进行了调整,以快速完成视频任务[29].
除了这些发展之外,VOS方法还依赖于密集的空间记忆,将物体跨帧连接起来并传播其面具[31、12、11、51、10、61]。
E-MAPS基于TinySAM的紧凑语义和即时前传,同时直接从事件流中学习时间动态.

blocks.en: 2.2 Event Representation Transfer and SAM Adaptation
blocks.zh: 2.2 事件代表转让和SAM适应

blocks.en:
Event segmentation spans event-native encoders, RGB-to-event transfer, and cross-modal fusion [ 44 , 1 , 49 , 55 , 56 ] .
EventSAM enables SAM-like event prompting through weighted distillation [ 9 ] , while SAM-Event-Adapter and EVSAM inject event cues into image models [ 53 , 14 ] .
MemorySAM applies SAM2-style memory to multimodal semantic segmentation, and other work studies language guidance and event-domain representation learning [ 28 , 24 , 23 , 8 , 34 ] .
These methods establish promptable event segmentation and cross-modal adaptation, mainly for per-window or multimodal prediction, while we seek to learn temporal dynamics under intermittent event streams.
blocks.zh:
事件分割跨越事件-事件编码器,RGB对事件传输,以及跨模式聚变[44, 1, 49, 55, 56].
EventSAM通过加权蒸馏促进SAM类似事件[9],而SAM-Event-Adapter和EVSAM将事件提示注入图像模型[53,14].
MemorySAM将SAM2风格的内存应用于多式联运语义分区,其他工作研究语言指导和事件域代表学习[28,24,23,8,34].
这些方法建立了快速的事件分化和跨模式的适应,主要用于每个窗口或多式联运预测,同时我们寻求在间歇事件流下学习时间动态.

blocks.en: 2.3 Event-based Video Segmentation and Tracking
blocks.zh: 2.3 基于事件的视频分割和跟踪

blocks.en:
ECOS is the closest event-only VOS predecessor, propagating an initial mask through recurrent event representations and cross-time matching [ 64 ] .
Event-assisted low-light VOS [ 26 ] and EVOLVE [ 2 ] instead combine frames and events through memory matching or dual-memory refinement.
Related work also studies event-guided video segmentation, frame–event instance segmentation, and high-rate tracking through frame–event fusion or RGB-to-event transfer [ 54 , 20 , 57 , 48 ] .
E-MAPS targets event-only mask propagation from point, box, or mask prompts, with arbitrary-window correction and object insertion.
blocks.zh:
ECOS是最接近事件唯一VOS的前身,通过经常性事件表示和交叉时间匹配来宣传初始面具[64].
事件辅助低光VOS [26] 和 EVOLVE [2] 转而通过内存匹配或双模完善将帧和事件结合起来.
相关工作还研究事件引导视频分割,帧-事件实例分割,以及通过帧-事件聚变或RGB对事件转移的高率跟踪[54,20,57,48].
E-MAPS目标只针对事件遮罩,从点,框,或遮罩提示进行传播,并带有任意窗口校正和对象插入.

Image encoder, prompt encoder, and mask decoder. We use TinySAM [ 41 ] for its efficient pretrained point-, box-, and mask-prompt interface. Temporal association is learned from scratch through the event memory described below. The image encoder processes 𝐗 t \mathbf{X}_{t} directly to produce shared feature embeddings.

To handle object absence and heavy occlusion, we add an occlusion token and a lightweight occlusion head following SAM2 [ 37 ] . The head is trained with focal loss using empty masks as absent-object labels.

blocks.en:
Memory-Aware Prompting (MAP). A key design choice is how to use retrieved object history to guide segmentation.
We explore three approaches: past-object feature fusion, dense memory cross-attention [ 37 ] , and prompt-based memory injection.
Past-object fusion uses only the latest stored object feature, removing temporal attention.
Dense cross-attention instead incorporates the event-derived memory readout through a randomly initialized SAM2-style decoder, without relying on RGB features or pretrained SAM2 memory weights.
As shown in Sec. 6.1 , prompt-based injection offers the best balance between segmentation accuracy and computational cost.
This design also fits naturally with the promptable decoder.
While the retrieved memory 𝐘 t ( k ) \mathbf{Y}^{(k)}_{t} contains dense object-conditioned information, the decoder receives object guidance through sparse prompts.
MAP bridges these representations by summarizing the retrieved history into K K memory prompt tokens 𝐓 t ( k ) ∈ ℝ K × C \mathbf{T}^{(k)}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times C} , where C C denotes the token width.

blocks.en: 5.1 Datasets and EViM construction.
blocks.zh: 5.1 数据集与EViM构建.

blocks.en: We build supervision from three complementary event sources. EOS [ 64 ] provides DAVIS-style sequences with native event-view instance masks. DSEC-Detection [ 19 , 18 ] provides real driving videos with dense boxes, class labels, and persistent track IDs. N-ImageNet [ 21 ] contributes broad semantic diversity through RGB–event pairs. Since DSEC-Detection and N-ImageNet lack instance masks, we construct and release E vent- Vi ew M asklets (EViM) using a semi-automated cross-modal annotation pipeline. EViM contains 206,811 RGB–event pairs and approximately 620K event-view instance masks. Table 1 compares EViM with prior datasets, which mainly provide semantic labels, image-level instances, or smaller video collections.
blocks.zh: 我们从三个互补活动来源建立监督。 EOS [64] 提供了DAVIS风格的序列,带有本土事件-视觉实例面具. DSEC-Detection [19, 18] 提供了真实的驱动视频,其中包含密集的盒子,类标签,以及持续的音轨ID. N-ImageNet [21] 通过 RGB-event 配对提供了广泛的语义多样性. 自DSEC检测和N图像以来 净缺乏实例口罩,我们使用半自动跨模式注解管道建造并释放E Express- Vi ew M asklets(EViM). EViM包含206,811个RGB–event对和约620K事件-视图实例口罩. 表1将EViM与之前的数据集进行比较,这些数据集主要提供语义标签,图像级实例,或较小的视频收藏.

blocks.en: EViM construction. For each RGB–event pair, an RGB teacher model generates candidate masks with confidence scores. Accepted masks are then transferred into the event-camera image plane. For teacher model, we consider large variants of SAM2.1 [ 37 ] and SAM3 [ 6 ] . SAM3 produces higher-quality masks, while cross-teacher agreement shows limited dependence on the selected teacher.
blocks.zh: EVIM建设. 对于每对RGB-事件,一个RGB的师范模型会产生有自信分数的候选人口罩. 然后接受口罩转移到事件-相机图像平面. 对于教师模型,我们考虑SAM2.1[37]和SAM3[6]的大型变体. SAM3生产质量较高的口罩,而跨教师协议显示对被选中的教师的依赖有限.

blocks.en: For DSEC-Detection, we prompt SAM3 on the synchronized RGB image using the ground-truth box and class text. We project each mask to the left event-camera view using the provided calibration. Masks are retained based on confidence and box–mask agreement, then grouped by track ID to form masklets.
blocks.zh: 对于DSEC-检测,我们用地面真实的框和类文本在同步的RGB图像上提示SAM3. 我们利用提供的校准将每个面具投射到左侧事件-摄像头视图。 面具根据信任和盒子-面具协议保留,然后按照音轨ID分组形成面具。

EViM benchmarks. We construct three fixed, training-disjoint benchmarks from the DSEC-Detection test split. EViM500 and EViM1000 respectively contain approximately 4.7K/3K clips and 47K/52K object instances, spanning 350–500 ms and up to 1 s. Their masks pass automatic QC and stricter human verification. blocks.en: 5.2 Quality control (QC)
blocks.zh: 5.2 质量控制(质量控制)

blocks.en: EViM combines automatic filtering with human verification. DSEC proposals are filtered using confidence and box–mask agreement, while N-ImageNet proposals are filtered using confidence and homography support. Reviewers then audit RGB–event–mask triplets for object identity, event-view alignment and geometric validity. In a final 2,000-triplet audit, 92.2% of post-QC masks are judged correct, while the hard failure rate decreases from 25.7% before QC to 4.8%.
blocks.zh: EViM将自动过滤与人类验证相结合. DSEC提案使用置信度和盒装任务协议进行过滤,N-ImageNet提案则使用置信度和图谱支持进行过滤. 审查者随后对RGB–event–mask三重机进行审核,以了解对象身份,事件视图对齐和几何有效性. 在2000年的最后一次三重审计中,有92.2%的QC后口罩被判定正确,而硬故障率则从QC前的25.7%下降到4.8%.

blocks.en: Training setup. We initialize the TinySAM image encoder, prompt encoder, and mask decoder from the public TinySAM checkpoint [ 41 ] , whereas RTEE, E2T, the memory module, MAP, and the occlusion head are randomly initialized and trained from scratch. Training follows the two-stage procedure in Sec. 4.4 : Stage I performs token-space alignment for 20 epochs with batch size 16, and Stage II trains clip-level propagation with memory prompting for 20 epochs using clips of 10 windows and memory window ( s s ) is 3. We take 384x384 event voxels and optimize with AdamW on two A100 80GB GPUs, using cosine learning-rate decay with a 5% linear warmup, weight decay 0.01, and betas 0.9, 0.999. Newly introduced modules use an initial learning rate of 3 × 10 − 4 3{\times}10^{-4} , while TinySAM-initialized modules start from 1 × 10 − 5 1{\times}10^{-5} .

blocks.en: Evaluation protocols. We evaluate four complementary settings on EViM and external benchmarks. EViM500, EViM1000, and EViM-HM are fixed, training-disjoint benchmarks using non-overlapping 50 ms event windows and reporting 𝒥 \mathcal{J} , ℱ \mathcal{F} , and 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} (Sec. 5 ). Quantitative tables mark the top three entries per column in red , green , and blue . In prompt-once VOS , a box initializes each object in its first annotated window for propagation without further interaction. In interactive ePVS , each corrected window receives three clicks. Online evaluation corrects predictions below 0.75 predicted IoU in a single pass, whereas offline evaluation first processes the sequence and then corrects the lowest-IoU windows under the same budget. FE108 [ 58 ] and VisEvent evaluate zero-shot event-based box tracking using success rate (SR). Zero-shot interactive tracking on VisEvent allows up to 3 3 corrections. Released checkpoints are used unless marked ft , indicating full-parameter finetuning on the same EViM split and event-window schedule. Recon. denotes E2VID [ 38 ] reconstructions.

Prompt-once VOS and efficiency. E-MAPS consistently achieves the highest 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} across EViM500, EViM1000, and EViM-HM, with scores ranging from 76.41 to 84.38.
Even after fine-tuning competing methods such as ECOS, SAM-I2V, and SAM2.1 B+, E-MAPS retains its advantage across all three benchmarks.
Beyond segmentation accuracy, E-MAPS offers substantial computational benefits.
E-MAPS runs at 27.41 FPS, over ten times faster than SAM2.1 B+, while requiring considerably fewer operations per frame.
Together, these results demonstrate that E-MAPS achieves accurate and efficient event-based tracking, with qualitative examples in Fig. 4 further illustrating its robustness under low-light conditions.

即时启动 VOS 和效率。 E-MAPS在EViM500,EViM1000和EViM-HM之间持续实现最高的J&F\mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F},得分从76.41到84.38.
即使在微调了ECOS,SAM-I2V,SAM2.1 B+等相互竞争的方法之后,E-MAPS仍然在所有三个基准中保持优势.
除了分解精度外,E-MAPS还提供了大量的计算效益.
E-MAPS的运行速度为27.41 FPS,比SAM2.1 B+快十倍以上,同时每帧的运行要求要少得多.
这些结果一起表明,E-MAPS实现了基于事件的准确有效的跟踪,图4中的质量实例进一步说明了其在低光条件下的稳健性.

blocks.en:
Interactive ePVS. E-MAPS consistently outperforms competing methods across all correction budgets in both online and offline protocols.
Performance improves steadily as additional corrections are introduced, with online 𝒥 & ℱ \mathcal{J}\&\mathcal{F} gains of approximately 2 points across all three benchmarks.
Offline interaction yields further improvements, reaching 87.08 on EViM500, 83.74 on EViM1000, and 79.89 on EViM-HM.
These results demonstrate that E-MAPS effectively incorporates new user prompts into its memory, allowing corrections to improve not only the current segmentation but also subsequent propagation.

这些结果表明,E-MAPS将新的用户提示有效纳入其内存,使更正不仅能够改进目前的分解,而且能够随后的传播。

blocks.en:
Zero-shot visual object tracking. To assess generalization beyond EViM, we evaluate E-MAPS without additional training on FE108 [ 58 ] and VisEvent.
Following [ 50 , 46 ] , tracking is initialized with a bounding box, and predicted masks are converted into tight bounding boxes.
On FE108, event-only E-MAPS achieves 70.15 SR, outperforming EventSAM+ECOS by 4.90 points while remaining competitive with RGB and RGB–event methods.
On VisEvent, it performs particularly well under challenging conditions, ranking first in low illumination (LI) and surpassing all RGB-only methods under fast motion and motion blur (FM+MB).
We further explore RGB–event fusion by averaging aligned TinySAM RGB and adapted event features [ 59 ] .
Despite its simplicity, this variant outperforms dedicated RGB–event methods under low illumination, occlusion (FOC+POC), and background motion and clutter (BOM+BC), while remaining competitive on FE108 and FM+MB.
These findings demonstrate that representations learned for ePVS transfer effectively to conventional visual object tracking.

零射视觉物体跟踪. 为了评估超越EViM的概括性,我们评价E-MAPS,而不进行FE108[58]和VisEvent的额外培训.
之后[50,46],跟踪用边框初始化,预测的口罩转换成紧边框.
FE108上,仅事件E-MAPS实现70.15SR,表现优于事件SAM+ECOS4.90分,同时保持与RGB和RGB-event方法的竞争.
在VisEvent上,它在挑战性条件下表现特别出色,在低射线(LI)中排名第一,并在快速运动和运动模糊(FM+MB)下超越所有仅使用RGB的方法.
我们通过平均对齐的TinySAM RGB和经过调整的事件特征,进一步探索RGB—事件聚变[59].
尽管它很简单,但这种变体在低光度、隐蔽(FOC+POC)和背景运动和杂交(BOM+BC)下比专用的RGB活动方法要好,同时在FE108和FM+MB上仍然具有竞争力。
这些调查结果表明,为电子光电学系统有效转移到常规视觉物体跟踪而学到的表述。

Zero-shot interactive tracking on VisEvent. We further evaluate how E-MAPS responds to user corrections without additional training.
The protocol allows up to three online box corrections whenever the predicted IoU falls below 0.5.

We measure the Success Rate before and after correction ( SR 0 \mathrm{SR}_{0} and SR 3 \mathrm{SR}_{3} ), with relative improvement defined as Δ rel = ( SR 3 − SR 0 ) / SR 0 \Delta_{\mathrm{rel}}=(\mathrm{SR}_{3}-\mathrm{SR}_{0})/\mathrm{SR}_{0} .
E-MAPS achieves relative gains of 15.3% overall and 30.8% under NMO conditions, substantially exceeding the improvements of both baselines.
These results highlight its ability to make effective use of sparse user corrections, particularly in challenging tracking scenarios.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: We introduced ePVS, where arbitrary-window prompts initialize, correct, or introduce objects and predictions form identity-consistent masklets. We presented E-MAPS, an event-only framework that retains pretrained semantic and prompting priors while learning propagation and correction directly from event masklets. E2T aligns recurrent event features with the pretrained representation space, while MAP converts object-conditioned history into sparse prompts, allowing memory and user inputs to share one efficient decoder pathway. We also introduced EViM for scalable representation transfer and event-video learning. We extensively evaluate E-MAPS across prompt-once and interactive ePVS, and zero-shot tracking on FE108 and VisEvent. These evaluations show that E-MAPS provides accurate and efficient segmentation from sparse event streams.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了ePVS,其中任意窗口会激发初始化,校正,或引入物体和预测,形成与身份一致的面具. 我们提出了E-MAPS,这是一个只针对事件的框架,它保留了事先经过训练的语义,并激发了前科,同时直接从事件面具中学习传播和校正。 E2T将经常事件特性与预先训练的表示空间对齐,而MAP将对象条件的历史转换为稀疏的提示,允许内存和用户输入共享一个高效的解码路径. 我们还引入了EViM,用于可伸缩性代表转移和事件视频学习. 我们广泛评价E-MAPS 跨即时和交互式ePVS,以及FE108和VisEvent的零镜头跟踪。 这些评价表明,E-MAPS提供了从稀少的事件流中准确而高效的分解.
